subject: Mid-contract capacity top-up, co-term and invoice cadence for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@nimbushealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Need mid-contract capacity top-up + co-term question

Hi Irene —

We hit an unexpected production ramp this month and will need roughly a 20% increase in reserved capacity starting June 1. We want to add the capacity mid-contract but co-term at our renewal on 2027-01-15. Two questions: can you provide (1) a top-up pricing estimate and (2) whether you can pro-rate the top-up so invoices align with our Qs (we prefer quarterly invoicing)? Procurement copied for visibility.

High-level numbers: current commit 1.0M tokens/month; target 1.2M tokens/month for 12 months (no change to model mix). We may be open to a 12-month add-on commit with a small uplift if there are credits/discounts in exchange.

Would love a quick pricing note today if possible — we need to loop legal and procurement this week.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of ML Ops
Nimbus Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Price <olivia.price@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need mid-contract capacity top-up + co-term question

Hi Olivia — thanks for the heads up and numbers. Short answer: yes, we can do a mid-contract top-up and co-term to your renewal; there are a couple of common approaches and trade-offs depending on how you want billing to behave. I’ve looped Ben (pricing lead) and Naomi (CS) — Ben will outline the pricing options and Naomi can confirm operational steps for onboarding the extra capacity.

Two quick clarifying points to help with precise math:
- Do you want the 20% bump to be committed for 12 months (preferred), or is it a temporary 3–6 month surge?
- When you say quarterly invoicing, do you want the top-up invoiced on the same quarterly cadence as existing charges or as a separate quarterly invoice?

I’ll get a short options memo back to you within the day.

Best,
Irene
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Price <olivia.price@nimbushealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Need mid-contract capacity top-up + co-term question

Hi Olivia — putting two pragmatic options on the table given your ask for a 20% bump. Attachment: Nimbus_Topup_Proposal_v1.pdf (contains line-item math).

Option A — Blended top-up (recommended if you want minimal billing churn)
- Add 200k tokens/mo to committed base for 12 months.
- Blended uplift: list uplift +15% applied to the top-up portion, with a 5% one-time onboarding credit to offset migration work.
- Co-term: we prorate remaining months to align new capacity to 2027-01-15; invoicing will be combined with your monthly statement (we can aggregate into quarterly invoices per your preference).

Option B — Standalone add-on (recommended if you want clean accounting)
- Add-on priced at list uplift (no blending) and billed separately quarterly.
- No onboarding credit. Co-term can be applied at renewal by converting the add-on into a committed block then.

Quick commercial note: if Nimbus agrees to a 12-month committed add-on (Option A), we can move to a milestone discount of 10% on the incremental units (effectively ~9.1% net on the top-up portion after the onboarding credit), contingent on signature within 7 business days.

Next steps: confirm preferred billing cadence (combined quarterly vs. separate), and whether Nimbus will sign a 12-month commit for the top-up. I can turn this into an amendment and DocuSign link once we have confirmation.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@nimbushealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need mid-contract capacity top-up + co-term question

Ben / Irene — thanks for the clear options. Procurement prefers a separate quarterly invoice for the add-on (Option B) to keep the POs distinct, but we’d be willing to convert to a committed 12-month add-on (moving toward Option A) if you can offer a guaranteed one-time onboarding credit and a shorter signature window.

Procurement asked: can you do a net ~8% discount on the incremental units if we sign a 12-month add-on and accept the separate quarterly invoice? Also please send any amendment language we should expect so legal can triage quickly.

Olivia

Quick internal note / recommended counter to present to Nimbus:

- Offer: 12-month committed add-on at +20% capacity (200k tokens/mo).
- Commercial: 10% discount on incremental units (this nets ~9% vs list) + a one-time onboarding credit equal to one month of incremental charges.
- Billing: keep as separate quarterly invoice for procurement, but include a short amendment that converts the add-on into the main commit at co-term (2027-01-15).
- Approval path: finance signs off on 10% discount if we can secure electronic signature within 5 business days. Legal needs amendment language; Naomi, can you generate a short ops checklist for onboarding?

If Nimbus accepts the above, we should be able to push the DocuSign envelope today and commit provisioning for 1 June.

—Marcus
